newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: Singapore rubber futures end down in thin trade.
newsitem.headline: Singapore rubber futures end down in thin trade.

text.p: Rubber futures finished lower on Friday in thin, lethargic trade as buyers shied away from the market, dealers said.

"There was just bits and pieces of buying here and there. But the volume in the market was very thin and we were just dying out there today," a rubber trader in a Singapore-based commodity house said.

"The market was flat. We also adjusted our prices lower after prices in Tokyo came off," another trader said. The benchmark July contract in Tokyo shed 1.6 yen to end at 156.0. Kobe's July contract inched up 0.2 yen to 155.7.
"It was very quiet all around," one dealer said.
The most actively traded contract was March RSS3 with about 500 tonnes traded.
At around 0945 GMT, April RSS3 was seen at 122.00-123.00 U.S. cents a kg from the previous 123.50 cents.
April RSS1 was seen at 174.00 Singapore cents (US$1.23) a kg from the previous 175.00 cents.
May TSR20 was seen at 168.50-170.50 Singapore cents (US$1.19-$1.21) a kg against 171.00 cents.
